text:
sam: Heads up — on prod we saw clients reconnecting within the grace window and generating duplicate billing events.
leah: ugh, which route? can you paste a trace id?
sam: route=streaming-edge-us-east-1, trace=6f3a9b2c... logs show resume token accepted then immediate reconnect
mike: paste logs? also what's the quota behavior — should resume be free when within grace?
sam: logs:
```
INFO resume accepted token=abc123
INFO connection closed (client): reason=socket_close
INFO new connection from same session, billing_event=charged
```
leah: looks like our resume handler accepts but doesn't mark session as in-flight so quota accounting treats it as new
jordan: is this specific to SSE or WS? we do slightly different handshake paths
sam: reproduces on both, but more frequent on SSE via proxy pool rotation
navya: console shows a single reconnect spike but per-token billing shows double for some users :thinking_face: 
mike: telemetry gap: do we have session_id -> route mapping in traces? might be a sampling issue
leah: we only attach session_id on endpoint accept; proxy-level resumptions bypass route tag sometimes
sam: proposal: when resume accepted, emit an idempotency marker and route claim event to metrichq
jordan: +1, but need to consider rollout UX — don't want a noisy new metric during canary
leah: we can gate metric behind flag and sample 100% for canary tenants (dedicated) and 5% for prod until stable
navya: also show a console annotation for resume-originated reconnects in route dashboard (new filter)
mike: implementer note: change in accounting window: treat resume within X seconds as no-charge, but need to define X (10s?)
sam: agreed. I'll open PR for marker + small docs change. cc @deploy-bot
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: patch/resume-idempotency-marker -> canary env at 2024-11-02T23:00Z :rocket:
leah: after canary we should run a synthetic to replay resume loops and verify no duplicate billing
sam: thanks all. I'll also attach a short query to surface affected tenant ids
navya: ty! :thumbsup:
